chapter: Last years of the band and reflections
title: Taxes, transportation costs and the end of the big bands
summary: A 20 percent tax on ballrooms and rising costs end the big bands, replaced by package shows.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But this is what broke the camel's back. And they had raised the tax on nightclubs and ballrooms 20 percent. Now, the Tunetown Ballroom owed a 20 percent tax. They just couldn't make it.
Meanwhile, the Internal Revenue closed it down, because they couldn't?
They hadn't paid the tax. They just couldn't make it. They finally took that tax off, but that's

what -- that was the beginning of the big bands going out, see. Transportation went up. It just cost too much money to transport a band around. Inflation was gradually moving in, even back then. Why, years ago, a band could come in or an out-of-town band could come in and you'd charge a dollar admission, which was a big price, but people could scuffle and get a dollar. But then, when you start bringing the bands in and charging more than a dollar, people just couldn't take it.

So then they started bringing in the big packages. They'd bring a big band in, they'd bring in some recording star with it. They would have a package deal with four or five attractions. Now, you don't have many of those now. You see what I mean? So this is what has happened.
